title: Output capture with isolation (foundational)
description: The program under test runs in a controlled harness that captures stdout, stderr, return code, and runtime. Capture is isolated so a crashing program cannot take the validator down with it. The captured bundle is the evidence the validator judges. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
import subprocess, sys
r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', 'print(40 + 2)'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
print('returncode:', r.returncode, '| stdout:', r.stdout.strip())
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Execution Result Validator practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Tolerance checking for numeric outputs (foundational)
description: Numeric outputs are compared with an explicit tolerance, absolute or relative, declared per requirement. Tolerance checking avoids false failures from floating-point representation, where 0.1 + 0.2 is not exactly 0.3. The tolerance used is recorded with the verdict. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
got, want, tol = 0.1 + 0.2, 0.3, 1e-9
print('within tolerance:', abs(got - want) <= tol, f'(tol={tol})')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Execution Result Validator practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Regression comparison against golden outputs (foundational)
description: Current output is diffed against a golden output recorded from a known-good run. Diffs are reported line by line so the change is visible, not just 'different'. Golden outputs are versioned with the program so the comparison stays meaningful as the program evolves. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
import difflib
golden = ['hits: 42\n', 'time: 0.4s\n']
current = ['hits: 42\n', 'time: 0.6s\n']
diff = list(difflib.unified_diff(golden, current, lineterm=''))
print('regression diff lines:', len(diff), '| sample:', diff[4].strip() if len(diff) > 4 else 'none')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Execution Result Validator practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Validation verdict with evidence (foundational)
description: The validator emits a verdict of pass or fail with every predicate result attached as evidence. A failing verdict names the exact requirement violated and shows the offending output. The verdict bundle is stored with the program version so validation history is complete. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
verdict = {'program': 'demo-1.0', 'predicates': {'contains_42': True, 'fast_enough': True}, 'verdict': 'PASS'}
print('validation verdict:', verdict['verdict'])
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Execution Result Validator practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.
